newsitem.title: USA: Peres sees next years as crucial for Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Peres sees next years as crucial for Mideast peace.

text.p: Israel Labour Party leader Shimon Peres said on Friday he saw a historic "window of opportunity" in the next four years to achieve a lasting, comprehensive peace in the Middle East.

In a speech to Jewish leaders meeting in Seattle, Peres said that between now and the end of the century the United States would remain in a unique position to help bring about peace in the Middle East as the world's only superpower.
But he said other potential superpowers such as China, Japan and the emerging united Europe were on the horizon, and he warned that by the end of the decade the world could be a far different place.

"1997 is going to be a crucial year for Jewish life and existence," he told the Council of Jewish Federations. "If the Jewish people would lose this window of opportunity our children would never forget it."

Peres described the past year as "probably the saddest year of my life," marked as it was by the assassination of his longtime comrade Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin followed by a series of deadly car bombs in the heart of Israel.
Peres said that despite repeated accusations he was a "traitor" he had continued with the peace process and a redeployment of troops from occupied territories.
"Can I describe it as a happy year? No. Do I have regrets? No. Because the alternative would be worse," he said.

While Peres said he remained opposed to the policies of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of the Likud Party, he told reporters that differences between Israelis and Palestinians in the current negotiations over the future of Hebron were very narrow and could be resolved relatively easily.
But he said continued negotiations for a comprehensive regional peace were crucial, including talks with Syria that would necessarily involve giving up part of the Golan Heights.
"Without a territorial compromise there will not be peace with the Syrians," he said. "We can postpone it for 10 years, but the price will not go down."
